videos.titulo: What is DEFY: four readings on one chart

cenas.fala: DEFY is a TradingView indicator that puts four readings on a single chart. The exhaustion bands show when price has stretched too far. The key levels mark where price has reacted before. The cloud tells you which way the market is pulling. And on top of it all, the idea: a card with the score and the plan drawn on the chart. In this video you'll see the first three pieces, exactly as they appear in the indicator.

First, the bands. There's a grey centre line, a smooth eighty-nine-bar average, and three bands on each side: inner, mid and outer. The upper ones are red, the lower ones blue, and the area between the mid and outer band is filled. Look at the end of the chart: the last stretch is dashed and fades out. That's the projection. DEFY estimates where the bands are heading, so you don't have to wait for them to settle.

itens: Price far from the centre line is stretched
Touching the opposite inner band is the stretch
Outer band: strong exhaustion, never a signal on its own
cenas.fala: How do you read them? When price moves far from the centre line, it's stretched, and a stretched market tends to come back. DEFY turns this into a rule: a buy idea is only born after price touches the lower inner band, and a sell idea after it touches the upper one. We call it the stretch. Without it, there's no idea. Reaching the outer band is strong exhaustion, but on its own it's never a signal.

The second reading is the key levels. DEFY finds tops and bottoms where price turned and merges the ones close to each other. Then it shows only the ten nearest to the current price, skipping any that would sit on top of each other, so the chart stays clean. Each level is a grey dashed line with a zone behind it: red if it's above price, blue if it's below.

The third reading is the cloud, built from two fast averages. Blue when the faster one is on top, red when it's below. The candles follow: blue in an uptrend, red in a downtrend, grey in transition. And there's one special candle, gold: a strong candle, with a big body and above-normal volume. You'll often see it at the moment of the idea.

itens: Cloud and candles: which way it pulls
cenas.fala: To recap: the bands tell you whether price has stretched, the levels show where it reacted, the cloud and candles show which way the market pulls, and the gold candle shows strength with volume. In the next video you'll see how these pieces add up to a score, and what the stars and the crown mean.

itens: At least three confirmations, after the stretch
cenas.fala: A DEFY idea never shows up by chance. It needs three things at once. A valid candle: a large body relative to the whole candle, and bigger than the previous ones. A close that breaks the last fractal, meaning the last small top in a buy, or the last small bottom in a sell. And at least three confirmations, after price has stretched to the inner band.

Look at the example. Price drops to the lower inner band, and the circle marks that touch. Right after, a strong gold candle appears and closes above the last small top. On that close, DEFY counts the confirmations and places the card below the candle, with the score.

The score starts at plus three, the minimum confirmations, and goes up one point for each confirmation in favour. There are fifteen possible: touches of the three bands, a key level nearby, the cloud and momentum in favour, the position against the averages, an engulfing candle, a rejection wick, a volume break, a fair value gap, a stretched RSI and a higher low. The gold candle adds one more.

cenas.titulo: Plus six, plus eight, plus ten

cartoes.d: Ten or more confirmations and a gold candle: King Idea

cenas.fala: The stars summarise the score. One star from plus six, two from plus eight, three from plus ten. And when there are ten or more confirmations and the signal candle is gold, the card turns gold with a crown: that's the King Idea. By default, DEFY only shows ideas of plus five and above, and you can raise that filter.

Here's a sell idea: the red card above the candle, with the score and the stars. After the idea, DEFY draws arrows over the next fifteen candles, whenever momentum stays in favour. That's the Trend Tracker: it shows whether the move still has strength.

cenas.texto: Stars measure confirmations. They don't guarantee the outcome.
cenas.fala: And remember: stars measure how many confirmations there are, they don't guarantee the outcome. A three-star idea can fail too, and that's what the plan is for. That's the topic of the next video.

videos.titulo: The plan in practice: entry, Warning, stop and targets

cenas.fala: When an idea is born, DEFY draws the full plan from the signal candle. The coloured zone runs from the entry to that candle's extreme: it's the momentum zone. And on the right are the labels with the prices: entry, Warning, stop and three targets, each with its distance in pips on forex or points on gold, indices and crypto.

linhas: close of the signal candle (or 50% in Pullback)
cenas.fala: The entry is the close of the signal candle. If you prefer, Pullback mode puts the entry at half the candle, and cancels the idea if price doesn't come back there within ten candles. The Warning is the signal candle's extreme: if price gets there, the idea is losing strength. The stop sits one ATR beyond the Warning. And the targets, in Standard mode, sit at one, two and three times the risk. There are also the Squeeze, Stretch and Swing modes, for targets on the bands or further out.

As the trade moves, DEFY marks each target hit with a tick on the label, and the arrows show whether momentum stays in favour. Alerts to your phone or to MoreThanMoney follow the same trade: entry, TP1, TP2, TP3 or stop.

And it fails too. Here the idea is born, price moves a little and then turns, passes the Warning and hits the stop, which gets a cross. It was a small loss, known before entering. That's exactly what the plan is for.

itens: Check the stretch and the stars
See if a key level is in the way
Set your risk per trade and size
Practise on a demo account first
cenas.fala: Before every idea: check the stretch and the score, see whether a key level sits between you and the targets, set your risk per trade and size the position. And practise on a demo account first. In the DEFY bootcamp, in this same playlist, we go deeper into each of these pieces.
